Jasmine / Lauren — below is a concise capacity playbook and sizing estimate based on Curelytics' profile. I kept assumptions explicit so sales/procurement can adjust.

Assumptions (from Thomas + conservative buffers):
- Model: LlamaX-70B tuned fork
- Context modes: 8k (95% of requests), 32k (5% of requests)
- Tokenization and effective token per request: avg 1.2k tokens for interactive flows; long-doc flows up to 32k tokens (rare).
- Concurrency: baseline 20, burst peak 120 (sustained ~15–45 minutes during peak).
- Target latency: 250ms/token interactive target (we use middle of their 200–350ms range).

Memory footprint (rough, per-GPU) — measured on A100-80GB equivalent baseline (FP16 runtime):
- Model weights (sharded across GPUs via tensor-parallel 8): ~8–10 GB per GPU (FP16).
- KV cache overhead: approx 0.35 bytes/token (model dependent) => 32k context ~11.2 MB per prompt per head? (we'll present safe estimate: 28–32 GB of KV per active session at 32k; with compression & chunking expect 18–24 GB).
- Working memory + activation buffers: ~8–12 GB per GPU when serving 32k slices.

Practical profiles (FP16):
- 8k context serving slice: 80–120 concurrent sessions per 1x 8-GPU pod (A100-80GB), but latency increases with synchronous decoding. For our latency target, estimate 8 GPUs to serve ~40 interactive streams at 250ms/token (conservative).
- 32k context: KV dominates. To maintain 250ms/token for 120 concurrent 32k sessions you'd need ~40 GPUs if you kept everything FP16 and memory-local. But since only 5% requests are 32k, a hybrid approach is far more cost-effective.

Recommended architecture (hybrid):
1) Reserved baseline pool (Dedicated) — supports normal traffic (95% 8k):
   - 2x 8-GPU pods (A100-80GB equiv) reserved = 16 GPUs total. Rationale: handles baseline concurrency (20 steady, ability to handle moderate burst to ~60) for 8k context at target latency while leaving room for routine autoscaling.
2) Burst/overflow pool — autoscale-enabled reserved burst capacity for spiky loads:
   - 1x 8-GPU pod on hot-standby for immediate bursts (adds headroom to ~100 concurrent 8k flows).
   - On predicted peak windows, enable cloud-bursting of additional 8–16 GPUs for 30–90 minute windows.
3) Long-context handling (32k) — specialized lane to avoid wasting baseline GPUs:
   - Run two NVMe-backed 8-GPU pods configured with KV offload and async IO. These pods are tuned for long-context jobs and serve as a separate queue. For the 5% long-context mix, 2 pods (16 GPUs) should handle concurrent long-doc requests without affecting interactive lanes.

Quantization impact & recommendations:
- int8 (post-training quantization) gains ~1.6–2x memory reduction for weights; runtime speedups depend on kernel support. For LlamaX-70B we expect ~35–50% inference cost reduction for 8k workloads with minimal quality drop for most prompts.
- For 32k context, KV cache is still dominant. Quantizing weights helps reduce GPU memory used for weights, but KV memory (cache) remains large; combine int8 + KV offload to NVMe for max cost savings.
- Conservatively: enabling int8 + KV offload reduces required GPUs for baseline by ~30–40% (so 16 GPUs -> ~10–12 GPUs) but increases per-request tail latency variability. Recommend offering two SKUs in the proposal:
   SKU A (higher quality / stable low-latency): FP16-only reserved pool (as above).
   SKU B (cost-optimized): int8 quantized weights + NVMe KV offload for baseline — suggested reserved 12 GPUs + same long-context pods (with offload) for peaks. Expect ~35% lower committed cost vs SKU A.

Fallback / degradation policy (SOP):
- Primary: route to reserved FP16 baseline.
- If baseline saturated: route new interactive sessions to quantized lane (int8) with notice header indicating slightly higher variance in outputs.
- If long-context queue backlogs: queue non-interactive jobs or shift to batched offline processing window; notify customer SLA contact and offer expedited burst at incremental charge.

Operational notes / runbook snippets:
- KV eviction: implement LRU with prefix caching for repeated sessions. Track per-customer KV use and evict longest-idle session pages first.
- Monitoring: token-level latency SLO dashboards, per-lane utilization, NVMe IO times, cache miss rates.
- Alerting: fire when baseline CPU/GPU utilization > 75% for >5 minutes, or long-context queue length > 10.

Preliminary sizing summary (conservative):
- SKU A (performance FP16): Reserved baseline = 16 GPUs (2x 8-GPU pods), Burst standby = +8 GPUs, Long-context pod = 16 GPUs (2x 8-GPU pods) => committed reserve ask: 32 GPUs.
- SKU B (cost-optimized int8 + NVMe offload): Reserved baseline = 12 GPUs, Burst standby = +8 GPUs, Long-context pod = 16 GPUs (offload-enabled) => committed reserve ask: 28 GPUs.

Cost/contract notes for sales:
- Recommend offering a 12-month reserved commitment with predictable monthly billing, and a separate burst/overage rate that is 1.5x standard unit price for on-demand GPUs during peak windows.
- Include an SLA clause for latency percentiles (p50/p95) tied to the SKU variant.

Open items / asks back to Curelytics:
- Confirm acceptable quality delta for int8 quantization on a 200-sample eval set (we can run quick eval in 48 hours).
- Confirm nightly offline ingest window tolerance (can we shift some long-context jobs to off-peak to reduce peak hardware needs?).

- Jasmine: share SKU A/B outlined above with procurement and indicate we can run an int8 quality eval ASAP.
- Dev: I'll prepare a short one-pager with the exact GPU counts, expected latency p50/p95 estimates, and a delta table for cost impact by SKU.

Plan to have the full doc for procurement by EOD Tue (18 Jun).
